A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same predictive-coding research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, component ablations, energy measurements and training-time comparisons on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and Tiny ImageNet.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds incremental-PC and ResNet results, targeted ablations, corruption evaluations and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: V3 introduces auxiliary neurons along residual connections to synchronize error propagation and extends the proposed training approach to incremental PC with within-inference weight updates (Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1). The original precision schedules, forward updates and BatchNorm freezing remain; decaying precision moves principally to Appendix D.1.

E1.justification: The classification datasets remain CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and Tiny ImageNet. V3 adds corrupted-input evaluation using six corruption types at five intensities on CIFAR10 (Appendix D.2.2), extending input-condition coverage. ResNet additions concern architecture settings rather than new datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds incremental PC, including centered-nudging comparisons in Figure 3, to the evaluated accuracy baselines and adds incremental-PC runtime comparisons in Table 7. The matched depth/nudging plot replaces decaying-precision variants with incremental-PC variants, although decay comparisons remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: The reported TPE search budget changes from 500 to 200 iterations (v1 Appendix A; v3 Appendix B). V3 adds ResNet configurations and relaxation-step ranges, corruption-calibration protocols, selective-layer forward-update controls and hyperparameter-transfer procedures. Its main benchmark also reports the best normalization configuration rather than separate normalization columns.

E4.justification: V3 adds auxiliary-neuron ablations, linear-decay comparisons, neural-divergence measurements and forward updates restricted to the last three layers (Tables 10–12). Corruption calibration, BatchNorm affine-parameter controls and hyperparameter importance/transfer studies substantially extend v1's component and energy analyses.

E5.justification: V3 introduces fANOVA-based statistical estimation of hyperparameter importance in Appendix E.1. Five-seed accuracy summaries and five-repetition timing measurements remain; the additional result rows do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive incremental-PC, ResNet and diagnostic results; Table 2 reports ResNet18/Tiny ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 57.83% for iPC plus spiking versus 58.18% for BP. Retained entries also change: non-BF VGG10/CIFAR100 S+F top-1 accuracy changes from 63.35 ± 0.12 to 69.08 ± 0.08 (v1 Table 1; v3 Table 8). This is a revised reported result, without evidence establishing a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V3 defines the Gap Ratio using initial-to-final neural-state divergence relative to layer update energy (Appendix D.2.1). It also removes v1's algebraic assertion that nudging can be reproduced by setting inverse output covariance to beta. The principal energy and precision equations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V1's central contribution concerns overcoming degradation in deep VGG-style networks. V3 adds residual-path timing as a third failure mechanism and claims successful ResNet18 training. It also makes incremental PC plus spiking precision central to its claim of backpropagation-comparable learning with operations local in space and time.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations involving asynchronous residual feedback, incremental updates reducing the need for forward updates, and different BatchNorm-freezing effects in PC and iPC. Appendix D.2.3 proposes free relaxation to recompute initial predictions, qualifying the storage-related biological-plausibility limitation. New robustness and hyperparameter-transfer findings receive substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 expands the pseudocode into explicit PC/iPC phases and documents ResNet blocks, channels, strides and relaxation ranges. Section 7 adds a promise to release code upon acceptance, without documenting an available release. Existing PCX, hardware, preprocessing and seed disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting incremental PC, incremental expectation-maximization, biological precision and free relaxation. Previously cited muPC receives an explicit comparison distinguishing its feedforward/MNIST scope, while several hardware and equilibrium-propagation references disappear. The broader PC/EP positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Methods are reorganized into algorithmic and structural contributions with embedded experiments, and the appendices are restructured into algorithm, settings, complexity, ablation and hyperparameter sections. Decaying precision and detailed benchmarks are relocated.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from four to seven panels, and Figure 4 combines a new residual-block diagram and auxiliary-neuron comparison with an expanded BatchNorm plot. Main benchmark tables are redesigned around additional architectures, while retained comparisons move to the appendix alongside numerous new diagnostic tables. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens v1's limited architectural validation and largely indirect mechanism evidence through residual-network interventions, incremental-PC comparisons, targeted forward-update controls and BatchNorm controls (Figure 4; Tables 10–12 and 16). Robustness and hyperparameter-transfer analyses further test applicability. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including the unexplained non-BF VGG10/CIFAR100 S+F top-5 discrepancy between Tables 8 and 15: 86.84% versus 88.66%.
